title: Drone Warp, Exposure Blend, and Sky Stitching in Photoshop (Moab Panorama)

date.basis: embedded_creation_time 2021-04-24T17:41:30.000000Z; transcript does not independently confirm the date.

locations.name: Moab, Utah, USA (explicit)
locations.basis: Transcript states 'downtown Moab' at the start.

summary: This instructional video demonstrates building an ultra-high-resolution drone panorama in Photoshop, starting from a nine-shot drone sequence stitched into a single panorama, then manually correcting misalignment with perspective and puppet warp. The presenter explains how to blend sky and landscape, balance exposure between different panels using RAW adjustments, and apply a sequence of color and light treatments (including blur-plus-luminosity diffusion, diffusion-based haze, and selective color) to create a cohesive final image with strong leading lines and a believable horizon. Throughout, the workflow emphasizes pre-stitch planning, careful sky replacement, and post-stitch refinements to preserve printability and avoid obvious seams, all demonstrated on a very large (approximately 170 MP) original capture.

sections.title: Initial panorama stitching and file organization
sections.description: The presenter describes using Photoshop's Photo Merge to create a base panorama from drone shots, noting that the original RAW files were stored separately and only JPEGs were used for the visible panorama in that moment.

sections.title: Perspective Warp and trapezoid alignment
sections.description: The video demonstrates flattening a stitched panorama, drawing custom trapezoidal boxes, and applying perspective warp to re-align edges so lines flow toward the center, discussing how wide-angle distortions affect corner geometry and the importance of trapezoidal corrections for seamless stitching.

sections.title: Puppet Warp for leading lines and final fit
sections.description: Puppet Warp is used to refine the alignment of image sections and enhance leading lines from the sides, with the operator describing how pins can warp or un-warp areas to achieve a visually pleasing crop and cohesive composition.

sections.title: High-resolution panorama and edge detail
sections.description: The narrator highlights the final panorama's extreme resolution (approximately 170 megapixels), discussing the level of detail and how 170 MP panoramas provide sharper imagery than typical camera sensors, reinforcing the incentive to stitch for maximum resolution.

sections.title: Second panorama stitch and sky-beam considerations
sections.description: The workflow repeats the stitching process for a separate sky shot, emphasizing the need to ensure sunbeams remain straight and to plan how skies blend with the landscape, noting that the sky can be warped to align with the center image if necessary.

sections.title: Sky patching with clone stamp and sky patch management
sections.description: A missing sky segment is addressed using the clone stamp to patch in sky, followed by flattening and expanding a sky piece to ensure a seamless blend between the sky and the landscape, including a workaround for an asset not present in the folder.

sections.title: Further sky warp and trapezoid-led adjustments
sections.description: Further perspectiveWarp steps are used to enlarge the sky area and produce stronger leading lines toward the sun, with notes on maximizing the effect while preserving printability.

sections.title: Balancing horizon exposure with RAW adjustments
sections.description: RAW adjustments are applied to both the landscape and sky to balance exposure, darken the horizon to match the sky, and reduce brightness differences, highlighting the grain discrepancy between drone JPEGs and camera RAWs and the need to pre-balance before final blending.
